---
title: "Join two tables"
---

Add each order's customer name and city from a customers table that shares
the `customer_id` column.

{{< include pages/_join.md >}}

- `left_join()` keeps every row of `orders` in its original order.
- An order with no matching customer gets NA in the new columns. A customer
  with no orders is left out.
- Each order gets one output row per matching customer. If `customers` had
  two rows for c1, each c1 order would appear twice.
- `relationship: 'many-to-one'` throws an exception when a key in `orders`
  matches more than one customer.
- `inner_join()` drops the orders with no match. `full_join()` also keeps
  customers with no orders and adds them after the matched rows.

Reference: [Joins, binding, and set operations](../reference/two-table.qmd#joins)
